learningObjectives: Explain what a Class is and why it reduces redundancy across TestSheets.
Create a Class using the two primary methods: manual creation and drag-and-drop from an existing Attribute.
Distinguish 'Create Class from Attribute' from 'Create Structure from Attribute'.
Resolve a reference before local customization and use Relevance to deactivate Attributes.

elements.description: A reusable Tosca object — conceptually similar to a Library in the TestCase section — that lets you define an Attribute structure (with its Instances and combinations) once and reuse it across many TestSheets via a Class Reference. A typical candidate is data that shows up repeatedly, like a Customer Attribute structure used by every TestSheet that touches customer data.

Class and reference editing are bidirectional: source changes update references, and editing an unresolved reference changes the corresponding Class. Resolve the reference first if you need an independent local variation.

bulletPoints: Class centralizes reusable Attributes and Instances.
Shared edits can affect all references; review consumers and their existing combinations.

elements.title: Creation methods
items: Manual: Create Class in a TestCase-Design folder (Ctrl+N, Ctrl+C); use a unique name and add Attributes/Instances.
Module: drag selected Module(s) onto the folder; Tosca creates a Class for each with relevant Attributes and Instances.
Attribute: drag selected Attributes onto the folder; the originals become Class references.

elements.term: Dragging an Attribute WITHOUT top-level combinations
elements.description: If selected Attributes have no child elements, the documented prompt offers Create Class from Attribute (Class plus Instance collection) or Create Structure from Attribute (Class without an Instance collection). The reference does not describe this as importing all source TestSheet combinations.

elements.text: Drag a Class onto a TestSheet, another Class or an Attribute to create its reference.

bulletPoints: The accessed page documents manual, Module and Attribute creation; an earlier Extract Class procedure was not verified.

elements.description: Once created, a Class can be modified exactly like a TestSheet — add or remove Attributes, create or delete Instances, adjust combinations, and set Character/Position on its Instances.

Resolve Class Reference removes the shared reference and returns it to an Attribute. Use this before making an independent local variation. Do not assume resolving one consumer removes other live references or makes deleting the source safe for all of them.

Unused combinations and deactivated Attributes are different concerns. Add the Relevance column, select a reference and disable the checkbox for an irrelevant Attribute. It becomes gray; F11 shows or hides deactivated Attributes. Deactivation is more than renaming or deleting a data value.

bulletPoints: Editing an unresolved reference updates its source Class.
Relevance is the documented column name; per-reference deactivation and visibility are distinct.

elements.text: Independent notes based on public 2026.1 documentation. The authenticated Academy video/exercises were not inspected; no guarantee is made about historical menu labels.

examPitfalls.title: Editing a Class Reference and expecting it to stay independent
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Changing a value inside a Class Reference and assuming other References to the same Class are unaffected.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Changes to an unresolved reference also change its source Class. Resolve the consumer before local customization and review other consumers before source deletion.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing 'Create Class from Attribute' with 'Create Structure from Attribute'
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming both options behave identically when converting an Attribute without existing combinations.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For selected Attributes with no children: Class creates an Instance collection, Structure does not. Do not infer automatic import of all TestSheet combinations.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming historical creation menus are current
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating an unverified Extract Class command as a required current method.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented manual, Module or Attribute workflows; check your installed version for additional commands.

examPitfalls.title: Mixing up bolded Instances with grayed-out Attributes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating 'bolded Instance' and 'irrelevant Attribute (grayed out)' as the same signal.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Relevance to deactivate Attributes in a reference, and F11 for visibility. Not using an Instance in a combination is a different operation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester updates the Class 'Customer Data', adding a new Instance. What happens to the TestSheets that already reference this Class?

options.text: Nothing — TestSheets must be manually refreshed one by one.
Each Class Reference automatically reflects the update, showing the newly created Instance.
Existing References break and must be recreated.
Only the first Reference created updates.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the core value proposition of using a Class in the first place.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documentation says Class changes update its references and reference modifications also change the Class. A new value is available to consumers; availability does not prove every existing combination uses it.

optionExplanations.A: The source/reference relationship updates shared data automatically.
optionExplanations.B: Class changes are reflected by references, though existing combinations still need review.
optionExplanations.C: A normal source edit does not inherently require recreating every reference.
optionExplanations.D: The documented behavior is not limited to the first reference.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Selected Attributes have no child elements. Which documented choice creates a Class with an Instance collection?
practiceQuiz.hint: The prompt distinguishes whether an Instance collection is created.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Create Class from Attribute creates a Class and Instance collection; Create Structure from Attribute creates a Class without the collection. This is not a guarantee of imported source TestSheet combinations.

optionExplanations.A: Structure creates a Class without the Instance collection.
optionExplanations.B: Class creates the collection for the specified childless-Attribute case.
optionExplanations.C: This is not the documented choice in that prompt.
optionExplanations.D: Resolving detaches an existing reference rather than creating a Class collection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester needs one reference to become independently editable while retaining its current structure. What is the documented action?

options.text: Delete the Class directly — References always keep a frozen copy automatically.
Select 'Resolve Class Reference' on that specific reference before removing the Class.
Rename the Class instead of deleting it.
Mark the Attribute as BusinessRelevant = No.

practiceQuiz.hint: Remove the shared reference before making an independent variation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Resolve Class Reference replaces the reference with an Attribute for local changes. Other consumers may still reference the original Class; review them before any source deletion.

optionExplanations.A: Deleting the source is not the documented independent-customization action.
optionExplanations.B: Resolving replaces the reference with an independently editable Attribute.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming preserves the shared reference relationship.
optionExplanations.D: Business relevance does not remove the source/reference link.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a Class Reference, an entire Attribute (not just one Instance) needs to be excluded from view for a specific TestSheet because it isn't relevant there. How is this done?

options.text: Delete the Attribute from the Class Reference.
Disable its Relevance checkbox for that Class reference; use F11 to show or hide deactivated Attributes.
Mark every Instance under it as Invalid.
This isn't possible — all Attributes in a Class Reference must always be shown.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is a per-Reference visibility setting, not a structural deletion.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented Relevance column controls per-reference Attribute deactivation. Deactivated Attributes are gray; F11 controls their visibility. This does not delete the source Attribute.

optionExplanations.A: Deletion would change shared structure rather than use per-reference deactivation.
optionExplanations.B: Relevance and F11 implement the documented deactivation/visibility workflow.
optionExplanations.C: Invalid labels expected input behavior, not Attribute relevance.
optionExplanations.D: The documentation explicitly permits deactivation and hiding.

quickRecap.value: Reusable Attribute structure (like a Library) — define once, use via Class Reference anywhere.
Documented manual, Module and Attribute workflows.

quickRecap.key: Create Class vs Create Structure from Attribute
quickRecap.value: For childless Attributes: Class creates an Instance collection; Structure creates none.
Replace the shared reference with an Attribute for local customization; other references remain shared.
Class updates affect references; unresolved reference edits affect the Class.
Deactivate referenced Attributes with Relevance; F11 controls their visibility.
